# Celmis

> Self-hosted code intelligence. Celmis indexes your repositories once and keeps a
> symbol graph of them; asking questions, reviewing pull requests, auditing
> dependencies and generating documentation are all different ways of reading that
> one graph. It runs on a single machine under `docker compose`, with the model
> provider of your choice behind it.

Licence: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0, with one exception noted in the
licence file. Source: https://github.com/Celmis-labs/Celmis

## What it does

- **Ask the code** — questions answered across several repositories at once, with
  file and line citations on every claim, including call chains that cross a
  repository boundary.
- **Pull-request review** — agents read the diff and, where the graph is built,
  who else calls what is being changed, including from another repository.
- **Dependencies, SBOM and evidence** — CycloneDX SBOM plus findings, a timeline
  and a manifest of sha256 digests, so a third party can verify the pack without
  trusting the machine that produced it. Celmis does not claim regulatory
  compliance on the operator's behalf.
- **Fix it from here** — a finding hands an embedded Claude Code session the
  repository, the package and the context; the runner pushes a branch and opens a
  pull request.
- **Access control** — per-repository visibility of none, metadata or code, with
  deny globs that win even at code level, so two teams can share an integration
  without sharing credentials.
- **MCP server** — eighteen tools over the same index, under the same access
  rules, for any MCP client.

## Measured facts

- 197 seconds from `git clone` to six healthy services on a clean server.
- $0.118 per pull request reviewed, on the model it ships with.
- 17th of 50 on the Martian Code Review Bench offline set, under all three judges.
  This measures pull-request review on isolated single-repository pull requests,
  a set with no sibling service for a symbol to have consumers in, so the
  cross-repository work the product is built around is absent from the number.
  Of the 79 findings the benchmark scored false, an audit found 33 were real
  defects the gold set was silent about.
- 23 languages parsed.

## Requirements

Docker 24+ with Compose v2, about 4 GB of free RAM, and an API key for one of
Google Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq or Mistral. Postgres and
Qdrant are bundled. Nothing is sent anywhere except the calls the operator
configures: no telemetry, no licence check.
